Problem This Solves\\n\\nOrchestrators (Kubernetes, Fly, Render, container platforms) have no probe that answers \\\"has the Gateway finished starting?\\\" without also folding in downstream channel takes an otherwise healthy Gateway and Control UI out of traffic rotation or blocks a rollout. There is also no HTTP surface exposing the running version, which makes \\\"which build is this deployment actually running?\\\" needlessly hard to answer for cloud operators.\\n\\nThe bundled deployment templates compound this:\\n\\n- `fly.toml` declared no health checks at all.\\n- `render.yaml` used `/health` (pure liveness) as Render's traffic-admission signal.\\n- The Kubernetes manifest combined the mutable `:slim` tag with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` (upgrades silently never happen) and an init container that unconditionally overwrote the persisted `openclaw.json` and workspace `AGENTS.md` on every pod start, erasing product-made edits.\\n- `docs/install/fly.md` still claimed the image `HEALTHCHECK` is pinned to port 18789; stale since `bc4221a07e9` (#116639) made `docker-healthcheck` resolve the active Gateway lock port.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nFirst step of the cloud-container deployment track: give every host one correct, additive probe contract before building anything platform-specific. `/readyz` semantics are a shipped public contract (existing manifests probe it), so this adds a probe rather than changing one.\\n\\n- New `/startup` + `/startupz` routes: `200 {\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"status\\\":\\\"started\\\"}` once startup work is complete and the Gateway is not draining; `503` with `status:\\\"starting\\\"` (plus `pendingReason` for privileged callers) during startup; `503` with `status:\\\"draining\\\"` during drain. Channel health is never consulted.\\n- The startup policy is one factory (`createStartupChecker`); the readiness checker now composes it instead of duplicating the startup/draining branches.\\n- Version (`resolveRuntimeServiceVersion`) and `uptimeMs` are included only for local-direct or authenticated callers, reusing the exact detail-gating already applied to `/readyz` subsystem names (now a shared helper). Remote unauthenticated probes get `{ok,status}` only — no build fingerprinting surface.\\n- Templates now use `/startupz` for startup/traffic admission, keep `/healthz` for liveness, and leave `/readyz` for channel-aware monitoring. K8s image pinned to the immutable `2026.7.1-2-slim` tag; init container seeds config only when missing.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\n- A failed channel account no longer evicts a healthy Gateway/Control UI from Service endpoints or fails platform health checks on the bundled templates.\\n- Operators and supervisors can read the running Gateway version over HTTP with their existing token (or locally) — no WebSocket handshake needed.\\n- Kubernetes deployments stop silently ignoring upgrades and stop losing config edits on pod restart.\\n- No behavior change to `/healthz`, `/readyz`, or any existing response shape. The browser permission call fires synchronously during an actively dispatching, direct, non-command composer gesture; subscription and Gateway registration continue asynchronously after permission is granted. If `revokeDeviceBootstrapToken` failed, the old single-use bootstrap token remained valid until expiration with no recorded diagnostic.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nThe QR fallback paths in `extensions/device-pair/index.ts` treated bootstrap token revocation and temporary QR directory cleanup as best-effort operations, but used empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers that hid failures from operators and logs. This change records a `warn` log for both failure modes so the issue is observable without blocking the setup-code fallback. Two regression tests verify the warning is emitted when revocation fails after QR delivery failure and after webchat QR render failure.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nOperators and developers can now see in logs when a bootstrap token revocation or QR temp cleanup failed during `/pair qr` fallback, making it possible to detect and respond to stuck security state instead of relying on the 10-minute token TTL to eventually expire the token.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n### Tests\\n\\n```bash\\nnode scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/index.test.ts\\n```\\n\\nResult: **67 passed** (2 new regression tests for revocation-failure logging).\\n\\n### Type check\\n\\n```bash\\npnpm check:test-types\\n```\\n\\nResult: passed.\\n\\n### Lint\\n\\n```bash\\nnode scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json extensions/device-pair/index.ts extensions/device-pair/index.test.ts\\n```\\n\\nResult: 0 warnings, 0 errors.\\n\\n### Before fix\\n\\n`extensions/device-pair/index.ts:895`, `:921`, and `:910` contained empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers:\\n\\n```ts\\nawait revokeDeviceBootstrapToken({ token: payload.bootstrapToken }).catch(() => {});\\nawait rm(path.dirname(qrFilePath), { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {});\\n```\\n\\nA failed revocation produced no log output.\\n\\n### After fix\\n\\nFailed revocation and cleanup now emit structured warnings:\\n\\n```ts\\nawait revokeDeviceBootstrapToken({ token: payload.bootstrapToken }).catch(\\n (revokeErr: unknown) => {\\n api.logger.warn?.(\\n `device-pair: failed to revoke bootstrap token (${String(revokeErr)})`,\\n );\\n },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n\\n### CI proof: device-pair revoke and QR cleanup warnings (with boundary run)\\n\\nProved this change at exact heads using a secretless GitHub Actions workflow that runs both an injected-runtime test and a boundary test (real plugin SDK channel runtime + real bootstrap-token state operations) against `main` (before) and the PR head (after). \"received_events_url\": \"https://api.github.com/users/steipete/received_events\", \"type\": \"User\", \"user_view_type\": \"public\", \"site_admin\": false }, \"body\": \"## What Problem This Solves\\n\\nOrchestrators (Kubernetes, Fly, Render, container platforms) have no probe that answers \\\"has the Gateway finished starting?\\\" without also folding in downstream channel health. `/readyz` flips to 503 when any channel account hard-fails (`blocked`, `terminal-disconnect`, post-grace `not-running` — `src/gateway/server/readiness.ts`), so one broken Telegram account takes an otherwise healthy Gateway and Control UI out of traffic rotation or blocks a rollout. There is also no HTTP surface exposing the running version, which makes \\\"which build is this deployment actually running?\\\" needlessly hard to answer for cloud operators.\\n\\nThe bundled deployment templates compound this:\\n\\n- `fly.toml` declared no health checks at all.\\n- `render.yaml` used `/health` (pure liveness) as Render's traffic-admission signal.\\n- The Kubernetes manifest combined the mutable `:slim` tag with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` (upgrades silently never happen) and an init container that unconditionally overwrote the persisted `openclaw.json` and workspace `AGENTS.md` on every pod start, erasing product-made edits.\\n- `docs/install/fly.md` still claimed the image `HEALTHCHECK` is pinned to port 18789; stale since `bc4221a07e9` (#116639) made `docker-healthcheck` resolve the active Gateway lock port.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nFirst step of the cloud-container deployment track: give every host one correct, additive probe contract before building anything platform-specific. `/readyz` semantics are a shipped public contract (existing manifests probe it), so this adds a probe rather than changing one.\\n\\n- New `/startup` + `/startupz` routes: `200 {\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"status\\\":\\\"started\\\"}` once startup work is complete and the Gateway is not draining; `503` with `status:\\\"starting\\\"` (plus `pendingReason` for privileged callers) during startup; `503` with `status:\\\"draining\\\"` during drain. Channel health is never consulted.\\n- The startup policy is one factory (`createStartupChecker`); the readiness checker now composes it instead of duplicating the startup/draining branches.\\n- Version (`resolveRuntimeServiceVersion`) and `uptimeMs` are included only for local-direct or authenticated callers, reusing the exact detail-gating already applied to `/readyz` subsystem names (now a shared helper). Remote unauthenticated probes get `{ok,status}` only — no build fingerprinting surface.\\n- Templates now use `/startupz` for startup/traffic admission, keep `/healthz` for liveness, and leave `/readyz` for channel-aware monitoring. \"user_view_type\": \"public\", \"site_admin\": false }, \"body\": \"Related: #111570\\n\\n## What Problem This Solves\\n\\nFixes an issue where operators who edit an agent's configuration while the gateway is running would keep getting the old configuration on every Feishu **group** message, while the same edit takes effect immediately in DMs and on the CLI.\\n\\nEditing `agents.entries[*]` (model, tools, and anything else the agent turn reads) is a hot reload: the gateway applies it and logs `config hot reload applied`. A Feishu DM sent right after picks up the change. A Feishu group message does not: it keeps running against the configuration captured when the channel account started, until the gateway or channel is restarted.\\n\\nA stale `tools.allow` surfaces loudly as `No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist`.\\n\\n**Correction (2026-08-12):** an earlier revision of this description also claimed a stale `model.primary` keeps serving the previous model, citing the second reporter on #111570. **I have since disproved that for current main**: see the gateway-boundary probe below. Model selection does not flow through the handler's config on this path, so it is unaffected by this change. The claim was wrong and is withdrawn.\\n\\nBecause the CLI runs in a fresh process and reads current config, the natural way to verify a fix (\\\"run `openclaw agent …` and see if it works now\\\") reports success while every inbound group turn keeps using the old config.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\n`handleFeishuMessage` received the configuration captured at account start (`startAccount` → `monitorFeishuProvider` → `monitorSingleAccount` → the handler, with no refresh anywhere in that chain) and only re-read the live snapshot inside an `if (isDirect)` branch. Everything a group turn resolves from that object (account resolution, group admission, model, tool policy) therefore came from the startup config.\\n\\nThe fix gives the whole turn one config identity at the entry point, so account resolution, admission, model, and tool policy all read the same live snapshot. This is the shape Telegram adopted in #103510 for the identical problem. It also means admission checks now run against current config rather than startup config, which is stricter than before, not looser.\\n\\nThat made the `if (isDirect)` refresh branch dead: `runtime.config.current()` is reference-stable (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.ts:11` returns `getRuntimeConfig`, asserted in `runtime-config.test.ts:31`), so its `currentCfg !== effectiveCfg` guard can no longer be true. It is removed in the same change. Net production delta is **−10 lines**.\\n\\nOne deliberate deviation to flag for review: `src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts:310` documents \\\"Prefer config passed into the active call path.\\\" Here the passed config *is* the stale value, which is why #103510 made the same deviation for Telegram.\\n\\nNot addressed here, recorded as follow-up: other channel adapters may carry account-start config into turns the same way, which is the audit @obviyus asked for on #111570. Also untouched: the broadcast adapter at `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` builds its turn from `cfg` rather than `effectiveCfg`; with this change both are live, but the asymmetry remains worth a separate look.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nEditing an agent's model, tool policy, or other `agents.entries` settings now takes effect on the next Feishu group message, the same as it already did for DMs and the CLI. No restart, no new configuration, and no operator action required. Behavior for DMs, and for anyone not editing config at runtime, is unchanged.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\nAdded a table-driven regression in `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` covering both chat types. It supplies an account-start config carrying `agents.list[0].model.primary = \\\"startup-model\\\"` and a live runtime config carrying `\\\"live-model\\\"`, dispatches one inbound message, and asserts which config reached agent dispatch.\\n\\nThe DM case is the control: it passes both before and after, which is what makes the group result meaningful: the harness can demonstrably observe a fresh config, so the group failure is a property of production code and not of the test.\\n\\n**Before**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`, exit 1:\\n\\n```\\n × dispatches group turns with the live runtime config 11ms\\nAssertionError: expected 'startup-model' to be 'live-model' // Object.is equality\\n Test Files 1 failed (1)\\n Tests 1 failed | 101 passed (102)\\n```\\n\\n**After**: same command, exit 0:\\n\\n```\\n Test Files 1 passed (1)\\n Tests 102 passed (102)\\n```\\n\\n**No regression**: `pnpm test:extension feishu`, run against a stashed baseline and against this change:\\n\\n| | total | passed | failed |\\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\\n| baseline (change stashed) | 1575 | 1574 | 1 |\\n| this change | 1577 | 1576 | 1 |\\n\\nThe one remaining failure is identical in both runs: `reply-dispatcher.test.ts > createFeishuReplyDispatcher streaming behavior > shows raw command detail in streaming card tool status`, already red on `main` at `fa03d9b913` and untouched here, so per `CONTRIBUTING.md` it is not addressed in this PR.\\n\\n`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files: exit 0.\\n\\nOne intermediate result worth reporting: a first attempt omitted the optional chain on `config?.current()` and broke 16 tests in `bot.broadcast.test.ts` (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'current')`), because several runtime doubles have no `config` slot and the previous DM-only call site never exercised them. The focused test file was green at that point; only the wider lane caught it.\\n\\n### Real-config proof (added after ClawSweeper review)\\n\\nThe evidence above was mocked end to end: `config.current` was a stub returning a literal, so it never exercised the production config path. Added `inbound runtime config freshness (real config file)`, which writes the hot-reloaded config to a **real file**, points the Feishu runtime at the production `getRuntimeConfig({ skipPluginValidation: true, pin: false })`, and asserts the group turn dispatches with the on-disk config. Only the Feishu transport and agent dispatch remain stubbed; the config plumbing under test is production.\\n\\nThat immediately surfaced something the stub had hidden: the real loader normalizes the legacy `agents.list` roster into keyed `agents.entries`. The stubbed config returned whatever literal the test wrote, so this transformation never ran. The assertion now reads both shapes, so it is about config identity rather than roster shape.\\n\\nRed/green for that case, against the same command:\\n\\n```\\n × a group turn reads the hot-reloaded config file, not the account-start snapshot 14ms\\n × dispatches group turns with the live runtime config 3ms\\nAssertionError: expected 'startup-model' to be 'live-model' // Object.is equality\\n Tests 2 failed | 101 passed (103) exit 1\\n```\\n```\\n Tests 103 passed (103) exit 0\\n```\\nRed was produced by checking out the pre-fix `bot.ts` from the parent commit, not by stashing. The fix is committed, so a working-tree stash was a no-op and initially produced a false green. Worth stating because that false green would have made the whole proof meaningless.\\n\\nFull lane after the addition: `pnpm test:extension feishu` → 1578 total, 1577 passed, 1 failed, the same pre-existing `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` failure as the stashed baseline. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed test: exit 0.\\n\\n### What could not be produced, and why\\n\\nA live-Feishu or mock-transport proof is not available to me here, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise:\\n\\n- There is no mock Feishu transport in this repo. `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/` covers `discord`, `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, but no `feishu`, and those adapters are **live** transports backed by `credential-lease.runtime.ts`, not mocks.\\n- A live proof therefore needs a real Feishu app, tenant, and group, which I do not have.\\n\\nThe nearest accepted precedent I could find for an external contributor on this channel is #103513, which ran the real production function against a local HTTP server standing in for the Feishu API and was rated `proof: sufficient`. The proof above follows the same principle, real production code path, stand-in only at the external boundary, applied at the turn-entry boundary this change touches.\\n\\n**A gateway-boundary probe is achievable, and here is the design.** After the second review I checked whether real Feishu ingress can be driven locally. It can, without credentials or network:\\n\\n- `monitorWebhook` opens **its own HTTP server** (`extensions/feishu/src/monitor.transport.ts:385`) on `webhookHost`:`webhookPort`, serving `webhookPath` (default `/feishu/events`).\\n- Webhook mode requires only `verificationToken` and `encryptKey` (`monitor.account.ts:519-523`); both can be arbitrary local values, and no outbound Feishu call occurs on that startup path.\\n- Request auth is `sha256(timestamp + nonce + encryptKey + rawBody)` in `x-lark-signature` (`monitor.transport.ts:113-116`), reproducible locally.\\n- The body is parsed as **plain JSON** (`parseFeishuWebhookPayload`, `monitor.transport.ts:84-91`); no AES envelope is needed, and dispatch runs with `needCheck: false`.\\n- From there it is the production path: `buildFeishuWebhookEnvelope` → `eventDispatcher.invoke(...)` → `handleFeishuMessage` → turn.\\n\\nSo a probe can boot a gateway with Feishu in webhook mode plus a mock provider, POST a signed group message, hot-reload the config, POST again, and observe **which model the provider is actually asked for** across the two turns. That is exactly the \\\"hot-reloaded gateway completing an inbound group turn\\\" the review asks for.\\n\\n### I built that probe. Here is what it showed, including what it disproved.\\n\\nThe probe boots a real gateway with Feishu active in webhook mode, POSTs a **signed** group message to the plugin's own ingress, hot-reloads config on disk, POSTs a second message, and records what the agent turn asks the provider for. The ingress half works exactly as designed:\\n\\n```\\n[feishu] starting feishu[default] (mode: webhook)\\n[feishu] Webhook server listening on 127.0.0.1:50899\\n[probe] signed webhook POST probe-msg-1 -> HTTP 200\\n[feishu] feishu[default]: received message from ou_probe_sender in oc_probe_group (group)\\n[feishu] feishu[default]: group session scope=group, peer=oc_probe_group\\n[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.model.primary)\\n[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.model.primary)\\n```\\n\\nSo signed ingress, group admission, a completed agent turn, and a real gateway hot reload all reproduce locally with throwaway credentials.\\n\\n**Then it disproved part of my own claim.** Using `agents.defaults.model.primary` as the observable, both branches produce the same result:\\n\\n| build | models the provider was asked for |\\n|---|---|\\n| with this fix | `[\\\"probe-startup-model\\\", \\\"probe-live-model\\\"]` |\\n| pre-fix `bot.ts` (parent commit) | `[\\\"probe-startup-model\\\", \\\"probe-live-model\\\"]` |\\n\\nIdentical. The reload applied in both runs and the fix was verifiably absent in the second, so **model selection does not travel through the handler's config here** and this change does not affect it. That is why the model claim above is withdrawn. Running the red case is the only reason I did not submit a probe that discriminates nothing.\\n\\n**Then I worked out exactly which config path this change can affect, by elimination.** Four observables, each run red/green against the same probe:\\n\\n| observable | outcome | why |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `agents.defaults.model.primary` | does not discriminate | resolved by core from the live snapshot, not from the handler's config |\\n| top-level `tools.allow` | does not discriminate | global policy, also resolved from the live snapshot |\\n| `agents.defaults.tools` | not a config key | `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: \\\"tools\\\"` |\\n| **`agents.entries.<id>.tools`** | **cannot be exercised in this harness** | see below |\\n\\nThe last row is the one that matters, because it is exactly what #111570 reports: the reporter's error reads `agents.main.tools.allow: message`. And it is the one path an ephemeral gateway structurally cannot reload:\\n\\n```\\n[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.entries.main.tools)\\n[reload] config reload failed: GatewayReloadRequiresRecoveryOwnerError: config reload requires a managed gateway restart owner for irreversible hot reload\\n```\\n\\n`shouldRefreshContextWindowCache` returns true for every path starting with `agents.entries.` (`src/gateway/config-reload-recovery.ts:98-108`), which makes the plan recovery-requiring; `assertIrreversibleReloadPlanHasRecoveryOwner` then throws unless `restartRecoveryAvailable`, which is `params.requestRecoveryRestart !== undefined` (`src/gateway/server-reload-managed.ts:62-63`). That emitter comes from a supervising service. The #111570 reporter ran a launchd-managed gateway and therefore saw `config hot reload applied`; a gateway started through `src/gateway/test-helpers.e2e.ts` has no recovery owner and the helper exposes no way to supply one.\\n\\n**So the accurate statement is not \\\"no observable effect\\\". It is that the only config path this change affects is the one my harness cannot reload, and that path is the reported symptom.** Everything else an ephemeral gateway *can* hot-reload turns out to be resolved by core from the live snapshot and is genuinely unaffected by this patch, which is worth knowing on its own.\\n\\n**This is cheap for a maintainer to settle.** On a managed gateway the same probe discriminates in one run: set `agents.entries.main.tools.allow` to a bogus tool, send a Feishu group message (fails with `No callable tools remain`), remove the allowlist, send another. Pre-fix the second message still fails; with this patch it recovers. I am happy to hand over the probe script, or to open it as the separate harness PR described below.\\n\\nWhat stands independently of that: the code-level asymmetry, group turns carry the account-start config while DMs refresh, which your review has now confirmed twice with `Findings: None`, plus the dead `if (isDirect)` branch this removes at net −10 production lines. If that is not enough on its own, I would rather you say so than have me keep dressing it up.\\n\\n**What I would rather not do is smuggle that harness into this PR.** The repo has no Feishu ingress test harness today, and the same gap blocks msteams, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.test-helpers.ts:189-204` builds `createActivityHandler` with `onMessage: () => handler`, discarding the message callback, so plain inbound messages cannot be driven there either. A harness that fixes this is shared infrastructure serving several channels, not a detail of this one-line-plus-deletion fix, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for one thing per PR.\\n\\nI am happy to build it as its own PR and then link it back here as the proof for this change. If maintainers would rather have it inline, or would rather apply `proof: override` given `Findings: None` / `Security: None` and the net −10 production delta, say which and I will follow.\\n\\n### Rebase and exact-head validation (2026-08-11)\\n\\nRebased onto `2cc11aff38` as requested; no conflicts, and neither changed file had been touched on main since the branch point.\\n\\n**The feishu lane is already red on that main.** `pnpm test:extension feishu`:\\n\\n| | total | passed | failed |\\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\\n| `2cc11aff38` (main, detached) | 1575 | 1547 | **28** |\\n| this branch rebased onto it | 1578 | 1550 | **28** |\\n\\nThe two failure sets are name-for-name identical (diffed), so this branch adds three passing tests and changes nothing else. Solves\\n\\nFixes Discord voice races where leaving during a pending join could reconnect later, a stopped session could subscribe after authorization, decoded STT work could outlive leave, followed-user state could resurrect an older move, realtime connect could report ready after close, and provider-reset completions could leak into a newer voice generation.\\n\\nThe previous voice implementation also concentrated connection, follow, receive, realtime, playback, turn, and consult ownership in two files over 4,000 lines, making these lifecycle invariants difficult to express and verify.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nThe voice subsystem is split by lifecycle owner into runtime, guild session, following, receive, realtime session, playback, turns, and consult modules. One per-guild generation now authorizes connection publication, capture, realtime state, transcripts, and playback; provider continuity retains its own epoch. Playback and exact-speech state are closed unions rather than parallel booleans.\\n\\nDiscord startup keeps its existing outer lazy boundary, while STT/TTS no longer loads realtime provider and consult machinery: `voice-session.ts` dynamically imports `realtime-session.runtime.ts` only for agent-proxy and bidi modes. Generic policy text and the exact-speech scraper remain byte-identical and are explicitly marked for a separate owner-reviewed realtime-voice follow-up.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nDiscord voice leave, follow, capture, and realtime operations are last-event-wins. Stale async work can no longer reconnect, subscribe, transcribe, play, publish readiness, or deliver provider completions after its voice generation has closed.\\n\\nThere is no configuration or Plugin SDK change. Existing voice instructions, consult/control tool schemas, transcript-source behavior, and STT/TTS behavior are preserved.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\nRegression provenance and before/after proof:\\n\\n- All six new order-sensitive regressions were run against the mechanical split commit and failed for the intended reason: pending leave (leave returned false), late receiver subscription, post-leave STT execution, stale followed-user publication, ready-after-close, and stale provider transcript delivery.\\n- The same six tests pass after the lifecycle-authority commit.\\n- Exact source comparison against pre-split `realtime.ts` confirms the assembled instruction builder and consult/control tool assembly are byte-identical.\\n\\nValidation on head `4119d4a90a416efa0ed2e2d70d62fc4849f88875`:\\n\\n- Focused lifecycle/follow/receive batch: 3 files, 100 tests passed.\\n- Focused playback/turns/consults batch: 3 files, 76 tests passed.\\n- Runtime composition E2E: join → audio ingress → agent dispatch → playback → leave passed.\\n- Full Discord batch: 220 files, 2,754 tests passed.\\n- Extension package boundary compile: 124 plugins passed.\\n- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <frozen-merge-base>`: green, including dead-code scans, production/test typechecks, extension lint, database-first guard, and zero runtime import cycles.\\n- `pnpm build`: green; no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warning.\\n- `pnpm lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`: green.\\n- `pnpm check:wrapper-shadowing`: green.\\n- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: green.\\n- `pnpm lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports`: green.\\n- `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`: green against the rebased branch base; the three superseded Discord voice entries were removed.\\n- Final branch autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; TruffleHog clean.\\n\\nRemote-proof note: Blacksmith Testbox was unavailable because the host lacks the `blacksmith` executable, and direct AWS Crabbox had no configured broker login. sessions and providers before they reached a model. A user-selected auth profile also collapsed same-provider auth routing to one candidate, so a second configured account was never tried.\\n\\nThis removes provider-failure control from command-lane capacity and makes a user auth pin a durable first preference instead of a strict singleton. Only the failed profile enters cooldown; eligible same-provider profiles remain available. Explicit provider/model selection stays strict.\\n\\n- keep quota/manual/circuit suspension markers for diagnostics and recovery, without changing lane concurrency\\n- try a valid user-pinned profile first, then ordered same-provider profiles\\n- skip only a cooled/disabled profile and return to the persisted pin after recovery\\n- preserve strict provider bindings and explicit provider/model selection\\n- include compatible external-CLI credential sources when discovering sibling profiles\\n- keep shutdown fencing for late suspension-marker writes\\n\\n## What Problem This Solves\\n\\nA failure on one provider credential must not pause unrelated work or suppress other authorized credentials for that provider. Before this change, one terminal quota failure could set a shared command lane to zero for 30 minutes, while a user-sourced auth override prevented the runner from trying a configured sibling profile.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n- Redacted live evidence showed one OpenAI quota failure setting the shared `main` lane to zero while an unrelated provider session waited before model invocation.\\n- Exact-head queue integration proves a suspension marker leaves unrelated `main`-lane work runnable.\\n- Exact-head runner E2E proves a user-pinned profile rotates to a same-provider backup in both OpenClaw and Codex harness paths, then surfaces failure only after all eligible profiles fail.\\n- Exact-head results: 314 focused tests and 47 runner E2Es passed; benchmark results are recorded below.\\n\\n## Root Cause\\n\\n### Before behavior\\n\\n1. `suspendSession` accepted a command-lane id, called `setCommandLaneConcurrency(lane, 0)`, and scheduled a default 30-minute resume timer.\\n2. Ordinary agent turns from different sessions and providers share the `main` lane. One terminal provider failure therefore blocked unrelated work at queue admission, before provider/model routing.\\n3. Runtime auth planning encoded a user-selected profile as required `user-lock` ownership. That produced one physical auth attempt and bypassed normal same-provider cooldown admission, even when another authorized profile existed.\\n4. External-CLI discovery also narrowed a user pin to one credential source before the planner could see ordered siblings.\\n\\nThe earlier repair in #93789 correctly deferred lane suspension while model fallback candidates remained, but terminal/direct failures could still lock a shared lane. The remaining invariant violation was architectural: provider/profile availability was controlling a process-wide scheduling primitive.\\n\\nThe Codex dependency contract confirms that one app-server client has one active `auth_manager`/account and surfaces usage-limit reset metadata. Cross-account selection is therefore OpenClaw's responsibility at its prepared profile/client boundary, not something one Codex client performs internally:\\n\\n- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2f108f9fd970ed73df7e984d3a661acc02f33abc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs#L818-L839\\n- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2f108f9fd970ed73df7e984d3a661acc02f33abc/codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs#L449-L550\\n\\n### RCA evidence\\n\\nA redacted production incident reproduced the complete ordering:\\n\\n- one OpenAI subscription profile returned a usage-limit error\\n- the exact profile received cooldown/reset metadata\\n- the terminal suspension path set the shared `main` lane to concurrency zero\\n- a separate session using an unrelated provider remained queued before any model call\\n- a second configured OpenAI profile was not attempted because the session auth override was user-sourced\\n\\nThe deployed base, active overlay patches, and persisted runtime state were inspected separately. Optional `renewStatus()` carries liveness additively.\\n\\nNo new config/default, protocol version, SQLite schema version, migration, alias route, command-version marker, or cross-process reconstruction layer is introduced.\\n\\n## Scope and remaining work\\n\\nThis PR fixes same-process and retained-client worker lifetime. on and miss agent completions.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nRequested by maintainer: auto-ask once on the first real prompt send, never re-ask after denial; Settings already surfaces the denied/blocked state as the manual repair path. The one-shot flag lives in per-origin `localStorage` because notification permission itself is per-browser/per-origin state. The browser permission call fires synchronously during an actively dispatching, direct, non-command composer gesture; subscription and Gateway registration continue asynchronously after permission is granted. Deferred catalog handoffs, Skill Workshop sends, widgets, and recognized commands cannot consume the one-shot. In the macOS app the same hook routes to the native permission prompt only while permission is `notDetermined`, and never auto-opens System Settings after denial.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nThe first real chat prompt in a supported, connected browser triggers the browser permission prompt; accepting registers the web push subscription immediately. Denying or dismissing means the browser is never auto-asked again; Settings -> Notifications continues to show status and blocked hints and remains the manual path. No new settings or configuration surface is added.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n- ClawSweeper-requested paired proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/notifications-auto-prompt.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-retained-presentation.test.ts` passed both shards: notification policy 18/18 (976ms) and retained-presentation handoff 7/7 (7.55s). Coverage proves the gesture fact is present during synchronous browser event dispatch and absent in the queued microtask, alongside permission, dismissal, direct composer, programmatic, command, disconnected, and empty-send cases.\\n- `pnpm docs:list` passed and indexed `web/notifications.md`.\\n- Local `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: conflict-marker check passed, but the max-lines ratchet raced an advancing `origin/main` and requested removal of baseline entries for `extensions/discord/src/voice/manager.e2e.test.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/voice/manager.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/voice/realtime.ts`, `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts`, and `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.ts`, all untouched by this PR. This change records a `warn` log for both failure modes so the issue is observable without blocking the setup-code fallback. Two regression tests verify the warning is emitted when revocation fails after QR delivery failure and after webchat QR render failure.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nOperators and developers can now see in logs when a bootstrap token revocation or QR temp cleanup failed during `/pair qr` fallback, making it possible to detect and respond to stuck security state instead of relying on the 10-minute token TTL to eventually expire the token.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n### Tests\\n\\n```bash\\nnode scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/index.test.ts\\n```\\n\\nResult: **67 passed** (2 new regression tests for revocation-failure logging).\\n\\n### Type check\\n\\n```bash\\npnpm check:test-types\\n```\\n\\nResult: passed.\\n\\n### Lint\\n\\n```bash\\nnode scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json extensions/device-pair/index.ts extensions/device-pair/index.test.ts\\n```\\n\\nResult: 0 warnings, 0 errors.\\n\\n### Before fix\\n\\n`extensions/device-pair/index.ts:895`, `:921`, and `:910` contained empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers:\\n\\n```ts\\nawait revokeDeviceBootstrapToken({ token: payload.bootstrapToken }).catch(() => {});\\nawait rm(path.dirname(qrFilePath), { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {});\\n```\\n\\nA failed revocation produced no log output.\\n\\n### After fix\\n\\nFailed revocation and cleanup now emit structured warnings:\\n\\n```ts\\nawait revokeDeviceBootstrapToken({ token: payload.bootstrapToken }).catch(\\n (revokeErr: unknown) => {\\n api.logger.warn?.(\\n `device-pair: failed to revoke bootstrap token (${String(revokeErr)})`,\\n );\\n },\\n);\\n```\\n\\n\\n### CI proof: device-pair revoke and QR cleanup warnings (with boundary run)\\n\\nProved this change at exact heads using a secretless GitHub Actions workflow that runs both an injected-runtime test and a boundary test (real plugin SDK channel runtime + real bootstrap-token state operations) against `main` (before) and the PR head (after). Solves\\n\\nOrchestrators (Kubernetes, Fly, Render, container platforms) have no probe that answers \\\"has the Gateway finished starting?\\\" without also folding in downstream channel health. `/readyz` flips to 503 when any channel account hard-fails (`blocked`, `terminal-disconnect`, post-grace `not-running` — `src/gateway/server/readiness.ts`), so one broken Telegram account takes an otherwise healthy Gateway and Control UI out of traffic rotation or blocks a rollout. There is also no HTTP surface exposing the running version, which makes \\\"which build is this deployment actually running?\\\" needlessly hard to answer for cloud operators.\\n\\nThe bundled deployment templates compound this:\\n\\n- `fly.toml` declared no health checks at all.\\n- `render.yaml` used `/health` (pure liveness) as Render's traffic-admission signal.\\n- The Kubernetes manifest combined the mutable `:slim` tag with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` (upgrades silently never happen) and an init container that unconditionally overwrote the persisted `openclaw.json` and workspace `AGENTS.md` on every pod start, erasing product-made edits.\\n- `docs/install/fly.md` still claimed the image `HEALTHCHECK` is pinned to port 18789; stale since `bc4221a07e9` (#116639) made `docker-healthcheck` resolve the active Gateway lock port.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\nFirst step of the cloud-container deployment track: give every host one correct, additive probe contract before building anything platform-specific. `/readyz` semantics are a shipped public contract (existing manifests probe it), so this adds a probe rather than changing one.\\n\\n- New `/startup` + `/startupz` routes: `200 {\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"status\\\":\\\"started\\\"}` once startup work is complete and the Gateway is not draining; `503` with `status:\\\"starting\\\"` (plus `pendingReason` for privileged callers) during startup; `503` with `status:\\\"draining\\\"` during drain. Channel health is never consulted.\\n- The startup policy is one factory (`createStartupChecker`); the readiness checker now composes it instead of duplicating the startup/draining branches.\\n- Version (`resolveRuntimeServiceVersion`) and `uptimeMs` are included only for local-direct or authenticated callers, reusing the exact detail-gating already applied to `/readyz` subsystem names (now a shared helper). Remote unauthenticated probes get `{ok,status}` only — no build fingerprinting surface.\\n- Templates now use `/startupz` for startup/traffic admission, keep `/healthz` for liveness, and leave `/readyz` for channel-aware monitoring. K8s image pinned to the immutable `2026.7.1-2-slim` tag; init container seeds config only when missing.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\n- A failed channel account no longer evicts a healthy Gateway/Control UI from Service endpoints or fails platform health checks on the bundled templates.\\n- Operators and supervisors can read the running Gateway version over HTTP with their existing token (or locally) — no WebSocket handshake needed.\\n- Kubernetes deployments stop silently ignoring upgrades and stop losing config edits on pod restart.\\n- No behavior change to `/healthz`, `/readyz`, or any existing response shape. No new config or env surface.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n- Regression proof: the new assertions fail on pre-change code (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts src/gateway/server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts` → 6 failed pre-fix, all for the missing routes/factory).\\n- Post-fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts src/gateway/server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts` green (output in PR checks / see below).\\n- New coverage: startup lifecycle transitions (starting → started → draining), hard channel failure flips `/readyz` but not `/startupz`, detail gating (remote unauthenticated gets minimal body; authenticated gets version/uptime/pendingReason), GET/HEAD parity with Content-Length, 404 on suffixed probe paths.\\n- K8s image tag verified against Docker Hub's exact-tag API (active amd64/arm64 manifest) and the `<release-tag>-slim` publication rule in `.github/workflows/docker-release.yml`.\\n- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/health.md` (probe table + semantics), `docs/install/{docker,fly,kubernetes,render}` including the corrected Fly healthcheck-port explanation.\\n\", \"created_at\": \"2026-08-12T06:05:25Z\", \"updated_at\": \"2026-08-12T06:38:21Z\", \"closed_at\": \"2026-08-12T06:36:35Z\", \"merged_at\": \"2026-08-12T06:36:35Z\", \"user_view_type\": \"public\", \"site_admin\": false }, \"body\": \"Related: #111570\\n\\n## What Problem This Solves\\n\\nFixes an issue where operators who edit an agent's configuration while the gateway is running would keep getting the old configuration on every Feishu **group** message, while the same edit takes effect immediately in DMs and on the CLI.\\n\\nEditing `agents.entries[*]` (model, tools, and anything else the agent turn reads) is a hot reload: the gateway applies it and logs `config hot reload applied`. A Feishu DM sent right after picks up the change. A Feishu group message does not: it keeps running against the configuration captured when the channel account started, until the gateway or channel is restarted.\\n\\nA stale `tools.allow` surfaces loudly as `No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist`.\\n\\n**Correction (2026-08-12):** an earlier revision of this description also claimed a stale `model.primary` keeps serving the previous model, citing the second reporter on #111570. **I have since disproved that for current main**: see the gateway-boundary probe below. Model selection does not flow through the handler's config on this path, so it is unaffected by this change. The claim was wrong and is withdrawn.\\n\\nBecause the CLI runs in a fresh process and reads current config, the natural way to verify a fix (\\\"run `openclaw agent …` and see if it works now\\\") reports success while every inbound group turn keeps using the old config.\\n\\n## Why This Change Was Made\\n\\n`handleFeishuMessage` received the configuration captured at account start (`startAccount` → `monitorFeishuProvider` → `monitorSingleAccount` → the handler, with no refresh anywhere in that chain) and only re-read the live snapshot inside an `if (isDirect)` branch. Everything a group turn resolves from that object (account resolution, group admission, model, tool policy) therefore came from the startup config.\\n\\nThe fix gives the whole turn one config identity at the entry point, so account resolution, admission, model, and tool policy all read the same live snapshot. This is the shape Telegram adopted in #103510 for the identical problem. It also means admission checks now run against current config rather than startup config, which is stricter than before, not looser.\\n\\nThat made the `if (isDirect)` refresh branch dead: `runtime.config.current()` is reference-stable (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.ts:11` returns `getRuntimeConfig`, asserted in `runtime-config.test.ts:31`), so its `currentCfg !== effectiveCfg` guard can no longer be true. It is removed in the same change. Net production delta is **−10 lines**.\\n\\nOne deliberate deviation to flag for review: `src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts:310` documents \\\"Prefer config passed into the active call path.\\\" Here the passed config *is* the stale value, which is why #103510 made the same deviation for Telegram.\\n\\nNot addressed here, recorded as follow-up: other channel adapters may carry account-start config into turns the same way, which is the audit @obviyus asked for on #111570. Also untouched: the broadcast adapter at `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` builds its turn from `cfg` rather than `effectiveCfg`; with this change both are live, but the asymmetry remains worth a separate look.\\n\\n## User Impact\\n\\nEditing an agent's model, tool policy, or other `agents.entries` settings now takes effect on the next Feishu group message, the same as it already did for DMs and the CLI. No restart, no new configuration, and no operator action required. Behavior for DMs, and for anyone not editing config at runtime, is unchanged.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\nAdded a table-driven regression in `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` covering both chat types. It supplies an account-start config carrying `agents.list[0].model.primary = \\\"startup-model\\\"` and a live runtime config carrying `\\\"live-model\\\"`, dispatches one inbound message, and asserts which config reached agent dispatch.\\n\\nThe DM case is the control: it passes both before and after, which is what makes the group result meaningful: the harness can demonstrably observe a fresh config, so the group failure is a property of production code and not of the test.\\n\\n**Before**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`, exit 1:\\n\\n```\\n × dispatches group turns with the live runtime config 11ms\\nAssertionError: expected 'startup-model' to be 'live-model' // Object.is equality\\n Test Files 1 failed (1)\\n Tests 1 failed | 101 passed (102)\\n```\\n\\n**After**: same command, exit 0:\\n\\n```\\n Test Files 1 passed (1)\\n Tests 102 passed (102)\\n```\\n\\n**No regression**: `pnpm test:extension feishu`, run against a stashed baseline and against this change:\\n\\n| | total | passed | failed |\\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\\n| baseline (change stashed) | 1575 | 1574 | 1 |\\n| this change | 1577 | 1576 | 1 |\\n\\nThe one remaining failure is identical in both runs: `reply-dispatcher.test.ts > createFeishuReplyDispatcher streaming behavior > shows raw command detail in streaming card tool status`, already red on `main` at `fa03d9b913` and untouched here, so per `CONTRIBUTING.md` it is not addressed in this PR.\\n\\n`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files: exit 0.\\n\\nOne intermediate result worth reporting: a first attempt omitted the optional chain on `config?.current()` and broke 16 tests in `bot.broadcast.test.ts` (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'current')`), because several runtime doubles have no `config` slot and the previous DM-only call site never exercised them. The focused test file was green at that point; only the wider lane caught it.\\n\\n### Real-config proof (added after ClawSweeper review)\\n\\nThe evidence above was mocked end to end: `config.current` was a stub returning a literal, so it never exercised the production config path. Added `inbound runtime config freshness (real config file)`, which writes the hot-reloaded config to a **real file**, points the Feishu runtime at the production `getRuntimeConfig({ skipPluginValidation: true, pin: false })`, and asserts the group turn dispatches with the on-disk config. Only the Feishu transport and agent dispatch remain stubbed; the config plumbing under test is production.\\n\\nThat immediately surfaced something the stub had hidden: the real loader normalizes the legacy `agents.list` roster into keyed `agents.entries`. The stubbed config returned whatever literal the test wrote, so this transformation never ran. The assertion now reads both shapes, so it is about config identity rather than roster shape.\\n\\nRed/green for that case, against the same command:\\n\\n```\\n × a group turn reads the hot-reloaded config file, not the account-start snapshot 14ms\\n × dispatches group turns with the live runtime config 3ms\\nAssertionError: expected 'startup-model' to be 'live-model' // Object.is equality\\n Tests 2 failed | 101 passed (103) exit 1\\n```\\n```\\n Tests 103 passed (103) exit 0\\n```\\nRed was produced by checking out the pre-fix `bot.ts` from the parent commit, not by stashing. The fix is committed, so a working-tree stash was a no-op and initially produced a false green. Worth stating because that false green would have made the whole proof meaningless.\\n\\nFull lane after the addition: `pnpm test:extension feishu` → 1578 total, 1577 passed, 1 failed, the same pre-existing `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` failure as the stashed baseline. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed test: exit 0.\\n\\n### What could not be produced, and why\\n\\nA live-Feishu or mock-transport proof is not available to me here, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise:\\n\\n- There is no mock Feishu transport in this repo. `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/` covers `discord`, `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, but no `feishu`, and those adapters are **live** transports backed by `credential-lease.runtime.ts`, not mocks.\\n- A live proof therefore needs a real Feishu app, tenant, and group, which I do not have.\\n\\nThe nearest accepted precedent I could find for an external contributor on this channel is #103513, which ran the real production function against a local HTTP server standing in for the Feishu API and was rated `proof: sufficient`. The proof above follows the same principle, real production code path, stand-in only at the external boundary, applied at the turn-entry boundary this change touches.\\n\\n**A gateway-boundary probe is achievable, and here is the design.** After the second review I checked whether real Feishu ingress can be driven locally. It can, without credentials or network:\\n\\n- `monitorWebhook` opens **its own HTTP server** (`extensions/feishu/src/monitor.transport.ts:385`) on `webhookHost`:`webhookPort`, serving `webhookPath` (default `/feishu/events`).\\n- Webhook mode requires only `verificationToken` and `encryptKey` (`monitor.account.ts:519-523`); both can be arbitrary local values, and no outbound Feishu call occurs on that startup path.\\n- Request auth is `sha256(timestamp + nonce + encryptKey + rawBody)` in `x-lark-signature` (`monitor.transport.ts:113-116`), reproducible locally.\\n- The body is parsed as **plain JSON** (`parseFeishuWebhookPayload`, `monitor.transport.ts:84-91`); no AES envelope is needed, and dispatch runs with `needCheck: false`.\\n- From there it is the production path: `buildFeishuWebhookEnvelope` → `eventDispatcher.invoke(...)` → `handleFeishuMessage` → turn.\\n\\nSo a probe can boot a gateway with Feishu in webhook mode plus a mock provider, POST a signed group message, hot-reload the config, POST again, and observe **which model the provider is actually asked for** across the two turns. That is exactly the \\\"hot-reloaded gateway completing an inbound group turn\\\" the review asks for.\\n\\n### I built that probe. Here is what it showed, including what it disproved.\\n\\nThe probe boots a real gateway with Feishu active in webhook mode, POSTs a **signed** group message to the plugin's own ingress, hot-reloads config on disk, POSTs a second message, and records what the agent turn asks the provider for. The ingress half works exactly as designed:\\n\\n```\\n[feishu] starting feishu[default] (mode: webhook)\\n[feishu] Webhook server listening on 127.0.0.1:50899\\n[probe] signed webhook POST probe-msg-1 -> HTTP 200\\n[feishu] feishu[default]: received message from ou_probe_sender in oc_probe_group (group)\\n[feishu] feishu[default]: group session scope=group, peer=oc_probe_group\\n[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.model.primary)\\n[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.model.primary)\\n```\\n\\nSo signed ingress, group admission, a completed agent turn, and a real gateway hot reload all reproduce locally with throwaway credentials.\\n\\n**Then it disproved part of my own claim.** Using `agents.defaults.model.primary` as the observable, both branches produce the same result:\\n\\n| build | models the provider was asked for |\\n|---|---|\\n| with this fix | `[\\\"probe-startup-model\\\", \\\"probe-live-model\\\"]` |\\n| pre-fix `bot.ts` (parent commit) | `[\\\"probe-startup-model\\\", \\\"probe-live-model\\\"]` |\\n\\nIdentical. The reload applied in both runs and the fix was verifiably absent in the second, so **model selection does not travel through the handler's config here** and this change does not affect it. That is why the model claim above is withdrawn. Running the red case is the only reason I did not submit a probe that discriminates nothing.\\n\\n**Then I worked out exactly which config path this change can affect, by elimination.** Four observables, each run red/green against the same probe:\\n\\n| observable | outcome | why |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `agents.defaults.model.primary` | does not discriminate | resolved by core from the live snapshot, not from the handler's config |\\n| top-level `tools.allow` | does not discriminate | global policy, also resolved from the live snapshot |\\n| `agents.defaults.tools` | not a config key | `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: \\\"tools\\\"` |\\n| **`agents.entries.<id>.tools`** | **cannot be exercised in this harness** | see below |\\n\\nThe last row is the one that matters, because it is exactly what #111570 reports: the reporter's error reads `agents.main.tools.allow: message`. And it is the one path an ephemeral gateway structurally cannot reload:\\n\\n```\\n[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.entries.main.tools)\\n[reload] config reload failed: GatewayReloadRequiresRecoveryOwnerError: config reload requires a managed gateway restart owner for irreversible hot reload\\n```\\n\\n`shouldRefreshContextWindowCache` returns true for every path starting with `agents.entries.` (`src/gateway/config-reload-recovery.ts:98-108`), which makes the plan recovery-requiring; `assertIrreversibleReloadPlanHasRecoveryOwner` then throws unless `restartRecoveryAvailable`, which is `params.requestRecoveryRestart !== undefined` (`src/gateway/server-reload-managed.ts:62-63`). That emitter comes from a supervising service. The #111570 reporter ran a launchd-managed gateway and therefore saw `config hot reload applied`; a gateway started through `src/gateway/test-helpers.e2e.ts` has no recovery owner and the helper exposes no way to supply one.\\n\\n**So the accurate statement is not \\\"no observable effect\\\". It is that the only config path this change affects is the one my harness cannot reload, and that path is the reported symptom.** Everything else an ephemeral gateway *can* hot-reload turns out to be resolved by core from the live snapshot and is genuinely unaffected by this patch, which is worth knowing on its own.\\n\\n**This is cheap for a maintainer to settle.** On a managed gateway the same probe discriminates in one run: set `agents.entries.main.tools.allow` to a bogus tool, send a Feishu group message (fails with `No callable tools remain`), remove the allowlist, send another. Pre-fix the second message still fails; with this patch it recovers. I am happy to hand over the probe script, or to open it as the separate harness PR described below.\\n\\nWhat stands independently of that: the code-level asymmetry, group turns carry the account-start config while DMs refresh, which your review has now confirmed twice with `Findings: None`, plus the dead `if (isDirect)` branch this removes at net −10 production lines. If that is not enough on its own, I would rather you say so than have me keep dressing it up.\\n\\n**What I would rather not do is smuggle that harness into this PR.** The repo has no Feishu ingress test harness today, and the same gap blocks msteams, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.test-helpers.ts:189-204` builds `createActivityHandler` with `onMessage: () => handler`, discarding the message callback, so plain inbound messages cannot be driven there either. A harness that fixes this is shared infrastructure serving several channels, not a detail of this one-line-plus-deletion fix, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for one thing per PR.\\n\\nI am happy to build it as its own PR and then link it back here as the proof for this change. If maintainers would rather have it inline, or would rather apply `proof: override` given `Findings: None` / `Security: None` and the net −10 production delta, say which and I will follow.\\n\\n### Rebase and exact-head validation (2026-08-11)\\n\\nRebased onto `2cc11aff38` as requested; no conflicts, and neither changed file had been touched on main since the branch point.\\n\\n**The feishu lane is already red on that main.** `pnpm test:extension feishu`:\\n\\n| | total | passed | failed |\\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\\n| `2cc11aff38` (main, detached) | 1575 | 1547 | **28** |\\n| this branch rebased onto it | 1578 | 1550 | **28** |\\n\\nThe two failure sets are name-for-name identical (diffed), so this branch adds three passing tests and changes nothing else. Before this change, one terminal quota failure could set a shared command lane to zero for 30 minutes, while a user-sourced auth override prevented the runner from trying a configured sibling profile.\\n\\n## Evidence\\n\\n- Redacted live evidence showed one OpenAI quota failure setting the shared `main` lane to zero while an unrelated provider session waited before model invocation.\\n- Exact-head queue integration proves a suspension marker leaves unrelated `main`-lane work runnable.\\n- Exact-head runner E2E proves a user-pinned profile rotates to a same-provider backup in both OpenClaw and Codex harness paths, then surfaces failure only after all eligible profiles fail.\\n- Exact-head results: 314 focused tests and 47 runner E2Es passed; benchmark results are recorded below.\\n\\n## Root Cause\\n\\n### Before behavior\\n\\n1. `suspendSession` accepted a command-lane id, called `setCommandLaneConcurrency(lane, 0)`, and scheduled a default 30-minute resume timer.\\n2. Ordinary agent turns from different sessions and providers share the `main` lane. One terminal provider failure therefore blocked unrelated work at queue admission, before provider/model routing.\\n3. Runtime auth planning encoded a user-selected profile as required `user-lock` ownership. That produced one physical auth attempt and bypassed normal same-provider cooldown admission, even when another authorized profile existed.\\n4. External-CLI discovery also narrowed a user pin to one credential source before the planner could see ordered siblings.\\n\\nThe earlier repair in #93789 correctly deferred lane suspension while model fallback candidates remained, but terminal/direct failures could still lock a shared lane. The remaining invariant violation was architectural: provider/profile availability was controlling a process-wide scheduling primitive.\\n\\nThe Codex dependency contract confirms that one app-server client has one active `auth_manager`/account and surfaces usage-limit reset metadata. Cross-account selection is therefore OpenClaw's responsibility at its prepared profile/client boundary, not something one Codex client performs internally:\\n\\n- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2f108f9fd970ed73df7e984d3a661acc02f33abc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs#L818-L839\\n- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2f108f9fd970ed73df7e984d3a661acc02f33abc/codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs#L449-L550\\n\\n### RCA evidence\\n\\nA redacted production incident reproduced the complete ordering:\\n\\n- one OpenAI subscription profile returned a usage-limit error\\n- the exact profile received cooldown/reset metadata\\n- the terminal suspension path set the shared `main` lane to concurrency zero\\n- a separate session using an unrelated provider remained queued before any model call\\n- a second configured OpenAI profile was not attempted because the session auth override was user-sourced\\n\\nThe deployed base, active overlay patches, and persisted runtime state were inspected separately. No overlay touched the causal lane-suspension/profile-planning ownership paths.\\n\\n## Real behavior proof\\n\\nClosest feasible environment: exact-head runner E2E with the real auth planner/controller and mocked provider transport, plus the real process command queue.\\n\\n```text\\n$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \\\\\\n src/agents/model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts \\\\\\n src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.run-embedded-agent.auth-profile-rotation.e2e.test.ts\\n\\nOpenClaw 2026.8.1 (82342d0)\\nTest Files 2 passed (2)\\nTests 47 passed (47)\\n```\\n\\nThe E2E matrix proves:\\n\\n- a rate-limited user pin rotates to the next same-provider profile\\n- the failed pin receives cooldown while the sibling succeeds\\n- a cooled pin is skipped on the next turn without replacing the persisted preference\\n- Codex-harness retry changes from the user-pinned OpenAI profile to the backup OpenAI profile and attributes the backup as automatic\\n- only after all same-provider profiles fail does the terminal failure surface\\n\\nThe queue integration proves an OpenAI suspension marker does not block unrelated `main`-lane work.\\n\\nPerformance benchmark: Node 25.9.0, same host/workload, 3 warmups plus 30 measured samples, using a 10 ms suspension TTL to measure unrelated `main`-lane admission.\\n\\n```text\\nbaseline ce53f7e82e2: median 10.181346 ms, p95 10.536215 ms\\nfinal 82342d00b00: median 0.012239 ms, p95 0.044799 ms\\n```\\n\\nThis measures removal of the artificial queue wait; it is not a provider latency benchmark.\\n\\n## What was not tested\\n\\n- The patched branch was not deployed to the production Gateway, and no real account was deliberately driven into quota exhaustion.\\n- Blacksmith Testbox validation was unavailable because its authentication had expired; AWS Crabbox was unavailable because the broker was not logged in.\\n- A full changed-file gate could not be cleanly reproduced in the linked worktree because its borrowed dependency tree carried unrelated terminal-core and generated Plugin SDK baseline failures.
